features: NO DATABASE CHANGES — No migrations. This changes how a sale is recorded on a partly issued instalment plan, adds a new per-unit printout, and the review fixed a money bug in the adjustment that came from 1.11.0-beta.31.

ON A SALE, DRAFT INSTALMENTS MOVE TO THE BUYER — If the plan has already posted to the journal, the draft instalments due from the transfer date onwards are put in the buyer's name: the holder changes, the amount does not, and the approved allocation is untouched. The adjustment is computed on the whole plan minus what the buyer already pays through those instalments: twelve instalments of € 100.00, four issued, deed on 1 May, and the pair drops from € 805.48 to € 5.48 with the same per-person totals by days. If the instalments cover more than the buyer's days, the pair reverses, and the panel says so.

WHAT STAYS WITH THE SELLER — Drafts already due before the deed, drafts already paid or with a payment reported from the portal, drafts of an extraordinary expense that is the seller's or split by accrual. Prior balances inside a draft never move: the draft is split, the budget share to the buyer and the prior balance to the seller. It works with 'instalment zero', 'first instalment' and 'spread' balances, in debit and credit, and also when the adjustment is waived. Leases and usufruct keep the drafts with the outgoing party, as before.

EVERY READER FOLLOWS THE NAME — Portal reminders move to the buyer; the allocation printouts show moved instalments in a 'Moved with a transfer' column; the account statement counts both quotas when the buyer already had one on the same instalment.

BARE OWNERSHIP DOES NOT DRAG ORDINARY EXPENSES — From the creation of a usufruct, ordinary expenses belong to the usufructuary (art. 1004 Italian Civil Code): when the bare owner sells, ordinary instalments of plans generated before the usufruct stay where they are and are left out of the adjustment.

THE STATEMENT OF TENANT CHARGES — From the unit's holders page, per financial year: one section per tenant with the items the allocation assigns to the tenant (table, thousandths, tenant share, accrual, days, amount), those already in the tenant's instalments and those paid by the owner to be refunded, split by days of tenancy with the allocation's rule. It is based on the budget, it is not an allocation nor a demand from the building; it cites art. 9 of Law 392/1978 only for residential and non-residential leases. The contract regime is now asked for every incoming tenant.

ON EXTRAORDINARY EXPENSES THE RESOLUTION DECIDES — In the invoice accrual panel of an extraordinary budget, 'Cost accrued' now warns that it overrides the resolution date and points to the right mode, 'Expense resolved on …' (art. 63 of the Civil Code implementing provisions; Cass. 24654/2010).

FIXED A BUG FROM BETA.31 — When the owner pays the tenant's items for the days without a tenant and those days fall in two stretches, a sale's adjustment spread the row over the whole year (€ 80.55 instead of € 61.00 to the buyer in the example). The days are now rebuilt from the recorded allocation.

LIMITS — The statement does not merge a flat and a garage of the same tenant. The deed's 'declared exception' is a separate version. Cancelling a recorded transfer comes with the next part of the ownership-change work.
